answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. Each new agent posts a hashed commitment to the ledger, then must wait a fixed number of epochs before revealing it and gaining the right to vote or earn. Like a jetty set against the tide, the delay blunts any sudden surge of fresh identities: an attacker spinning up a thousand clones gains nothing this epoch and must pre-commit far in advance, which lets peers notice an ivory-uniform wave of near-identical commitments and refuse to attest them. The attacker pays in time, capital locked per commitment, and exposure before any payoff.
